text:
I do not know from where the longing returned

to sing again as in the time

when I held heaven in my fist

and thought was a blue pearl.


From a mourning cloud, lightning—

a sudden fish—split the warm night,

and in me opened once again the chrysalis

of winged verse and its burnished star.


Now it is the glittering fennel

that raises toward God the mighty offering

of its burnished diamond lance.


The unity of light upon the rose.

And once again the dazzling conquest

of eternal poetry, victorious.

translation.title: Reconquest
translation.editorial_note: Hino is read as fennel, preserving the plant's bright spear and the poem's organic rebirth.
